messages.subject: group model returns warning that: "variance-covariance matrix of the estimated parameters (vcov) does not appear to be positive definite!"
parts:
Hi I have a model with two dichotomous exogenous variables (Function and Condition) , two latent mediator variable(CC and AS) (each has three measured variables) and one final outcome variable (proka). I have the data in two groups with 154 and 128 observations. My model specification is as under:

model2 <- '
#latent variables
CC =~ CC1 + CC2 + CC3 
AS =~ AS3 + AS4 + AS5

#Regressions
CC ~ a*Function + d*Condition 
AS ~ b*Function + e*Condition  
proka ~ j*Function + k*Condition + g*CC + h*AS  

#correlation
AS ~~ CC
Function ~~ 0*Condition'

I need to check for measurement invariance. As a first step, when I run the group based model without fixing loadings or intercepts, I get this warning: The variance-covariance matrix of the estimated parameters (vcov) does not appear to be positive definite! The smallest eigenvalue (= -4.004031e-17) is smaller than zero. This may be a symptom that the model is not identified.. I used this code: 
fit <- cfa(model2, data = exp2, estimator = "WLSMV", group = "group")

However, when I run the model separately for the two groups, or fix the loadings, the model runs normally. Am I doing something wrong? What should I do to address this and manage to do the measurement invariance test? (I guess when I fun the fit model without fixing anything, there are double the number of parameters to be identified as compared to a single group - so if this is true, how do I still manage to check for invariance?)

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: group model returns warning that: "variance-covariance matrix of the estimated parameters (vcov) does not appear to be positive definite!"
parts: Piyush--
1. the two exogenous variables (Function and Condition) are both dichotomous. Therefore I use WLSMV. Is this correct?

No. If you treat Function and Condition as covariates--meaning basically that they are observed variables and predictors only--these dichotomies do not violate the assumptions behind maximum likelihood (ML) estimation. ML only assumes normality conditional on the covariates. I believe that, if you simply omitted your syntax's reference to the covariance of Function and Condition, lavaan's default would be to treat those variables as covariates.

     The provided outputs make reference to a list of 8 "defined parameters," but I do not see these parameters defined in your "Model2" syntax, from your previous message. You name some parameter estimates, but you do not define new parameters. Where do those additional defined parameters come from? They could be implicated in the error message that you are receiving,

     I am also surprised by your "SEM-MI.png" output, which shows the results of the measurement invariance function. This output shows the configural invariance model to have 40 degrees of freedom, consistent with the multiple group models that you show elsewhere.
     The next step, imposing invariant loadings, gains 12 degrees of freedom. I find that surprising, since I see only 6 loadings to be estimated in the model (times 2 groups), and some of those are already fixed to 1. So I cannot myself understand where the gain of 12 degrees of freedom comes from.
     Then, in the following step, which imposes invariant intercepts, degrees of freedom increase by only 5. That is extremely odd--typically, we would expect the gain from constraining loadings and the gain from constraining intercepts to match, unless there is some peculiar specification.

     I believe that I would like to see the syntax that actually produced these results, including the creation of the new "defined parameters."

--Ed Rigdon

parts:
On 5/7/20 11:36 AM, Piyush Shah wrote:
> I have been trying on my own, have not been able to make it work. Is
> there some problem with making meanstructure = TRUE in WLSMV? So, when I
> run the model for one group (Group A) as
>
>     fit_a <- cfa(model2, data = exp_a, estimator = "WLSMV")
>
> it works. But when I run it as
>     fit_a1 <- cfa(model2, data = exp_a, estimator = "WLSMV",
> meanstructure = TRUE)
>
> I get the same warning message: In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel2,
> lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :
> lavaan WARNING:
> The variance-covariance matrix of the estimated parameters (vcov) does
> not appear to be positive definite! The smallest eigenvalue (=
> -4.042715e-16) is smaller than zero. This may be a symptom that the
> model is not identified.

Why are you using WLSMV? If your endogenous variables are continuous,
use ML. Even if your covariates (Function and Condition) are binary.

If you have binary variables, but you treat them as continuous, AND you
ask for the meanstructure, then your model will not be identified, as
the variance of a binary variable is a function of its mean. This
results in a non-positive definite variance/covriance matrix for the
model parameters. Hence the warning.

Yves.
